benefits: Lowest cost per GB for long-term data preservation
description: Move historical or rarely accessed data to low-cost archival storage.
disadvantages: Data must be identified and classified before archiving
name: Archiving
not_recommended_when: All data needs to be accessible with low latency
Retention period is less than 1 year

benefits: Handles traffic spikes via cache absorption
description: Store frequently accessed data in a fast in-memory cache to reduce database load and response latency.
disadvantages: Stale data risk without proper TTL strategy
name: Caching
not_recommended_when: Data changes on every read (no repeat reads)
Write-dominant workload with negligible read traffic
Dataset is small enough to fit in database memory

description: Split large files into smaller fixed-size or content-defined chunks for efficient storage and transfer.
disadvantages: Adds metadata overhead for chunk tracking
name: Chunking
not_recommended_when: Files are small (under 10 MB)
Simple object storage handles the workload adequately

benefits: 10-100x faster analytical queries vs row-oriented storage
Reduces I/O by reading only needed columns
description: Store data in column-oriented format for efficient analytical queries that scan specific columns.
name: Columnar Storage
not_recommended_when: Workload is purely transactional with no analytics
Queries always fetch full rows

benefits: Reduces storage footprint by 30-70% depending on data type
Improves I/O throughput for sequential reads
description: Reduce data size using lossless or lossy algorithms to lower storage costs and improve I/O throughput.
disadvantages: May increase latency for random access patterns
Compression ratio varies significantly by data type
name: Compression
not_recommended_when: Data is already compressed (images, videos in compressed formats)
Ultra-low latency random reads are required and CPU budget is tight

benefits: Reduces compute cost for repeated reports
description: Pre-aggregate raw data into summary tables for faster reporting and dashboards.
disadvantages: Loss of granularity in aggregated data
Cannot answer ad-hoc queries on raw data
name: Data Aggregation
not_recommended_when: Users need access to raw granular data
Query patterns are unpredictable

benefits: Improves query performance on smaller datasets
description: Remove or archive obsolete, expired, or irrelevant data to reduce dataset size.
disadvantages: Requires clear retention and pruning policies
name: Data Pruning
not_recommended_when: Regulatory requirements forbid deletion
All data has ongoing business value

benefits: Significant storage reduction when duplicate data is common
description: Eliminate redundant copies of data to reduce storage consumption.
disadvantages: Risk of hash collision (extremely rare but not zero)
name: Deduplication
not_recommended_when: Data has very low redundancy (unique sensor readings, time-series)
Startup team lacks operational capacity for dedup infrastructure
Budget does not support the additional compute

benefits: Orders-of-magnitude faster lookups on indexed columns
description: Create database indexes to accelerate read queries on frequently accessed columns.
disadvantages: Increases write latency (index maintenance on every write)
name: Indexing
not_recommended_when: Write-heavy workload where every millisecond of write latency matters
Queries are analytical scans rather than point lookups

benefits: Automated cost optimization without manual intervention
Reduces operational burden of data management
description: Automate data transitions between storage tiers and eventual deletion based on age or access patterns.
disadvantages: Requires clear lifecycle rules and policies
Misconfigured policies can delete data prematurely
name: Lifecycle Management
not_recommended_when: No clear data aging pattern exists
All data must be retained at the same tier indefinitely

benefits: Provides near-instant response for pre-computed queries
description: Pre-compute and store query results for expensive aggregations or joins.
disadvantages: Refresh strategy needed (stale vs fresh trade-off)
Not suitable for highly dynamic data
name: Materialized Views
not_recommended_when: Underlying data changes every second and views must be fresh
Query patterns are unpredictable (ad-hoc exploration)

benefits: Low cost per GB compared to block or database storage
description: Store unstructured data (images, videos, documents) in a scalable object store rather than a relational database.
disadvantages: Higher latency than local/block storage for small objects
Not suitable for transactional or relational queries
name: Object Storage
not_recommended_when: All data is purely structured/transactional with no binary objects

benefits: Column pruning for efficient analytical queries
Broad ecosystem support (Spark, DuckDB, Pandas, Athena)
description: Use Apache Parquet columnar file format for efficient analytical data storage and processing.
disadvantages: Not suitable for low-latency point queries
Requires tooling that supports the format
name: Parquet Format
not_recommended_when: Data requires frequent row-level updates
No analytical workload exists

benefits: Dramatically faster queries that match the partition key
Improved write throughput via partition-level locking
description: Divide large tables into smaller partitions based on a key (date, region, ID range) to improve query performance and manageability.
disadvantages: Schema changes can be more complex
name: Partitioning
not_recommended_when: Dataset is small (under 10 GB)
Queries rarely filter on the partition key

description: Analyze and rewrite slow queries, optimize execution plans, and eliminate unnecessary operations.
disadvantages: Benefits are workload-specific and not always predictable
name: Query Optimization
not_recommended_when: Queries are already optimized
Performance bottleneck is not in the database layer

description: Maintain copies of data across multiple nodes or regions for availability and read scaling.
disadvantages: Replication lag can cause stale reads
Write throughput is limited by synchronous replication
name: Replication
not_recommended_when: Single-node availability is acceptable
Budget cannot support multiple database instances

description: Redesign database schema for query efficiency: normalize or denormalize based on workload patterns.
disadvantages: Requires deep understanding of query patterns
name: Schema Optimization
not_recommended_when: Schema is simple and queries already perform well
Workload is purely write-heavy with minimal reads

benefits: Each shard handles a fraction of total load
description: Distribute data across multiple database instances based on a shard key for horizontal scaling.
disadvantages: Cross-shard queries are expensive or impossible
name: Sharding
not_recommended_when: Single database can handle the load
Team lacks experience with distributed databases
Cross-shard joins are frequently needed

benefits: Significant cost reduction by moving cold data to cheaper storage
Maintains fast access for frequently used data
description: Separate data across hot, warm, and cold storage tiers based on access frequency.
disadvantages: Retrieval from cold tiers may have higher latency
Migration policies need monitoring and tuning
name: Tiered Storage
not_recommended_when: All data is accessed uniformly with no clear hot/cold boundary
Retention is very short (under 6 months)
